item.text: I found the scan warning list (`o.warns`). I’ll record each source filename error there and leave the binary package in the scan results. I’ll also make the filename splitter carry a numeric epoch into the parsed version, with both RPM input paths avoiding a duplicate epoch in the source version.

The parser changes and regression tests are in place. The tests cover a malformed source filename, an epoch-prefixed source filename, continued scanning across multiple lines, source to binary links, and the repoquery path. I’ll format the files and run the existing scanner tests with dependency downloads disabled.

The targeted scanner test run is still compiling dependencies and has produced no result yet. I added a repoquery epoch case while it runs, since that path has its own source package construction. I’ll rerun the targeted tests after compilation if this run started before that case was added.

The scanner test command is still running without output, and the diff has no whitespace errors. The code review shows that a source filename error now adds a warning while returning the binary package; the scan loop can then continue to later lines. I’m waiting for the test result before closing this out.

item.text:
Updated [the RPM parser](/app/scanner/redhatbase.go) so an unparseable source RPM filename adds a warning and leaves the binary package available for analysis. Epoch-prefixed source filenames now produce the correct source name and version without duplicating the epoch.

Added regression tests in [redhatbase_test.go](/app/scanner/redhatbase_test.go). The targeted parser tests and the full `scanner` test suite pass.
